title: PeerBand relay WebSocket messages
description: Text frames (UTF-8 JSON, at most 65536 bytes) exchanged on wss://<server>/connections after the client authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer <installation credential>`. A client that streams agent events also sends `x-peerband-features: events` on the upgrade request. Discriminator: the `type` field. Binary frames are protocol errors; receivers ignore frame types they do not know.

event.title: client -> server: agent event
event.description: Pushed by the client when an agent changes, so MCP clients and the dashboard read output only when something happened. Metadata only: events never carry terminal output; `agent.notified` carries a short sanitized note for the machine owner. Sent only while the socket is open (never queued); after every (re)connect the client sends one `agents.changed` so consumers resync. The client coalesces bursts (at most one `agent.status_changed` per agent per 250 ms, latest wins) and caps its overall event rate. The envelope (eventId, name, timestamp, data) is shaped so it can be forwarded as MCP events later.

eventId.description: Random UUID v4, unique per event.

timestamp.description: When the client observed the event, ISO 8601 in UTC.

agentStatusChanged.title: data of agent.status_changed
agentStatusChanged.description: `agentId`, `label` and `workspace` are the values list_agents reports for the agent. `previousStatus` is null when the client had not seen the agent before; `revision` is the runtime's revision counter for the agent when known.

agentsChanged.title: data of agents.changed
agentsChanged.description: Agents appeared, exited or changed occupant (or events may have been missed): consumers should call list_agents again.

agentNotified.title: data of agent.notified
agentNotified.description: A note sent with `peerband notify` from inside an agent's pane. `agentId` is that agent, or null when it could not be identified. The text is stripped of control characters and passed through the client's secret redaction. It is meant for the machine owner only (`audience`), optionally addressed to one of their channels (`channel`).

channel.description: Optional (`peerband notify --channel`): the name of one of the owner's webhook endpoints. The note always appears on the machine's event stream (and so in the dashboard). Of the owner's webhook endpoints, only the named one receives it when `channel` is present; when absent, every endpoint that takes notes does. Servers that do not know the field may ignore it.

request.title: server -> client: tool request
request.description: At most 32 outstanding per connection; the client answers within 15 seconds. Requests are never replayed.

args.description: camelCase arguments: list_agents {machine, workspace, status, cursor, limit}; get_agent_status {agentId}; get_agent_output {agentId, lines, bytes, cursor}; send_agent_message {agentId, message, idempotencyKey}; get_request_status {requestId}.

role.description: owner: the caller owns this machine; guest: the caller reaches it through a share. The client treats a missing or unknown role as guest when it labels delivered messages.

email.description: The caller's account email, when the server knows it. Omitted otherwise.

ping.title: server -> client: heartbeat
ping.description: Sent after 20 seconds of silence. The client must answer with pong; the server closes with code 4000 if no pong arrives for 60 seconds. The client must treat any ping with extra keys as a request-shaped violation (closes 1007).

response.title: client -> server: tool response
response.description: Exactly one of `result` or `error`. `id` echoes the request id.

$comment: Close codes: 1000 normal; 1007 invalid JSON/message (client); 1008 policy or duplicate request id (client); 1009 frame too large; 4000 heartbeat timeout; 4001 replaced by a newer connection for the same installation; 4401 authentication failed (also HTTP 401/403 on upgrade). The client treats 4001, 4003, 4401 and HTTP 401/403 as terminal (revoked) and stops reconnecting.
